column1: # BnF fr. 3315 f. 21r, the cipher slip pasted over Renato Birago's clear Italian letter of 28 Sept 1574: cipher signs,
# line by line and word by word, read from Gallica image f23 (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF, ark btv1b90600800, full size, crops).
# 14 Nov 2026, Claude (session of 14 Nov 2026). A single AI transcription, not checked by a person.
# The slip is in the cipher of the duchess's letter on ff. 15-16 (same signs, same French interlinear decipherment
# hand), NOT a cipher of Birago's Italian letter. Checked by decoding with f15_key.md: see f21_slip_decryption.md.
# Notation as in f15_signs.tsv: 1=a  ±=b  C=c  b=d  F=e  +=f or m  0=g  h=h  7=i/j  3=l  2=n  8=o  G=p (looped)
#   9=q or s  T=r  4=t (also the q-like "et" form)  6=u/v  Z=x/z  y=y  ʒ=doubling sign (ss)  b̶=crossed d (ll)
#   s = word-final s written as a 6 with a raised hook (vous, lors, pas, Nemours)   SS=Roy   [-d-]=Royne (crossed sign)
#   ? after a sign = doubtful sign   {...} = words written in clear on the cipher line   [struck] = struck-out signs
